quiz.question: In Python, the call range(1, 5) produces the sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
quiz.explanation_correct: range(start, stop) generates numbers from start up to but NOT including stop, so range(1, 5) produces 1, 2, 3, 4 only.

explanation_wrong.True: This is incorrect because range() stops BEFORE the stop value — 5 is excluded, so the sequence is only 1, 2, 3, 4.

quiz.misconception_targeted: Believing range(start, stop) includes the stop value.

quiz.explanation_correct: range(2, 10, 3) starts at 2, adds 3 each step, and stops before reaching or passing 10. So it produces 2, 5, 8 (the next value, 11, would exceed 10, so it stops).

explanation_wrong.2 5 8 11: 11 is not included because it is greater than or equal to the stop value, 10. range() always stops before reaching the stop value.
explanation_wrong.2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9: This would be the result if the step were 1, but the step here is 3, so numbers are skipped between values.
explanation_wrong.3 6 9: This ignores the start value of 2; the sequence must begin at the specified start, not at a multiple of the step.

quiz.misconception_targeted: Confusing step behavior with start value, or thinking stop is inclusive.

quiz.explanation_correct: range(10, 0, -2) starts at 10, decreases by 2 each time, and stops before reaching or passing 0, producing 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 in that order.
range(1, 5) only produces 1, 2, 3, 4 because the stop value is exclusive. To include 5, the stop argument must be 6, i.e., range(1, 6).
quiz.misconception_targeted: Assuming the stop value in range() is included in the output.
